props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · nearest filter · one shader · value swept by script
props.title: Which Cell, and Where in It

B01.capture_spec: C01: Lab sprite scene (teal test sprite, scale to fit), lab-shaders/01-showcase.gdshader with the uniform phase swept linearly 0 to 1 over 12 s (--animate phase:0:1), 30 fps, Forward+, nearest filter, no input. At 50 %: all four panels visible, pixelation mid-way. At 85 %: blocks coarse, dots mid-swell.
B01.visual_intent: Act title 'Which Cell, and Where in It' (serif 40) top-left. A real Godot render in a framed window on the cream stage: one square split in four panels, all drawn by one shader: top left the teal test sprite going from smooth to chunky blocks, top right a teal-and-cream checkerboard scrolling, bottom left gold-and-cream diagonal stripes sliding, bottom right a grid of teal dots that swell and shrink. One-word labels land beside each panel as the voice names it.
B01.motion_claim: All four panels are alive at once: blocks coarsen, the checkerboard scrolls, the stripes slide, the dots pulse.

show.event: label 'blocks' beside the top-left panel
label 'checker'
label 'stripes'
label 'dots'
label 'one trick' under the whole square

B01.runner_up: manim drawing of four small pattern icons
B01.why: The claim is that one shader draws four different effects; only a real render of all four at once, moving, shows that. A drawing would only assert it.

B02.visual_intent: The series ramp strip across the stage (a bar of light-to-mid greys, never near-black), end labels 0 and 1, caption 'UV.x' above it. It stretches: the right end label counts 1, 2, 3, 4 and the caption becomes 'UV.x × 4'; vertical tick lines grow at 1, 2 and 3, cutting the bar into four spans, and the whole numbers 0, 1, 2, 3 appear under the left end of each span. Midpoint still (45 to 55 %): the strip is stretched and labelled 0 to 4, caption 'UV.x × 4'; the ticks have not appeared yet.
B02.motion_claim: The right label counts up to 4 while the ticks grow at each whole number.

show.event: ramp strip, labels 0 and 1, caption UV.x
right label counts to 4; caption becomes UV.x × 4
ticks at 1, 2, 3; span numbers 0 to 3

B02.why: The idea is the whole numbers appearing along the ramp; a render would show a gradient but not where the whole numbers fall.

B03.visual_intent: The same ramp, now 0 to 4 with ticks at 1, 2, 3 (cast continues). A terracotta dot rides it with a live value above it; at the right a large readout 'floor = 0' (monospace) steps up only when the dot crosses a tick. The dot pauses at 0.7 (readout shows 0.7 and 0), runs on, pauses at 2.9 (readout shows 2.9 and 2). The span under the dot is underlined by a terracotta bar. Label under the bar: 'floor: rounds down'. Midpoint still (45 to 55 %): the dot is settled at 2.9 with the readout 'floor = 2' (it runs there between 36 and 44 %); the label 'floor: rounds down' is on screen.
B03.motion_claim: The dot slides and the floor readout changes only at the ticks: 0, 1, 2, 3.

show.event: dot at 0.7, floor = 0, span 0 underlined
label 'floor: rounds down'; the dot holds at 0.7: readout 0.7 gives 0
the dot runs on quickly to 2.9, the readout stepping 1, 2 as it crosses the ticks (finished by 44 %)
span 2 underlined; the cell numbers 0, 1, 2, 3 light in turn

B03.why: The claim is 'which step you are on': a dot crossing ticks with a readout that changes only there says it directly; a staircase plot comes next, for fract.

B04.visual_intent: Axes on the cream stage: x from 0 to 4 along the bottom with ticks at the whole numbers, y from 0 to 1. A terracotta dot travels along x and draws the sawtooth of fract(x) behind it: a ramp from 0 to 1 that drops back to 0 at each whole number. At x = 2.9 the dot pauses at height 0.9 with the label 'fract(2.9) = 0.9'. The formula 'fract(x) = x − floor(x)' sits above the plot. Midpoint still (45 to 55 %): the dot is paused at 2.9, height 0.9, with the label 'fract(2.9) = 0.9'; the curve is drawn as far as 2.9.
B04.motion_claim: The curve draws itself, climbing from 0 to 1 and snapping back to 0 at every whole number.

show.event: axes; the sawtooth starts to draw; formula above
dot pauses at 2.9, height 0.9, label fract(2.9) = 0.9
the last teeth draw; every drop marked at a whole number

B04.runner_up: ramp strip with a second strip below
B04.why: A sawtooth is the exact picture of 'climbs, then starts over'; two strips would hide the reset.

B05.visual_intent: A square 4 by 4 grid of outline cells at left (no fill behind text), column numbers 0 to 3 along the top, row numbers 0 to 3 down the left side. A terracotta dot travels to the point 2.3 across and 1.7 down. Cell (2, 1) gets a heavy outline. At right, that one cell is magnified as a unit square with the dot inside it. Labels: 'cell (2, 1)' beside the grid and 'inside (0.3, 0.7)' beside the magnified cell. Midpoint still (45 to 55 %): the dot sits at (2.3, 1.7), cell (2, 1) has its heavy outline and the label 'cell (2, 1)'; the magnified cell has not opened yet.
B05.motion_claim: The dot lands, its cell lights up, and the cell opens out to show where inside it the dot sits.

show.event: grid; dot travels to (2.3, 1.7)
cell (2, 1) outlined; label 'cell (2, 1)'
cell magnified, dot inside; label 'inside (0.3, 0.7)'

B05.why: A dot with both numbers read off live is the idea; the two spoken pairs land on two visible labels.

B06.capture_spec: C02: Lab sprite, white 128 px texture (--sprite-tex white), lab-shaders/02-cells-floor.gdshader, still PNG. Verified: 16 distinct colors; cell (0,0) = 0.25, 0.25, 0.55; cell (3,3) = 1.0, 1.0, 0.55; every pixel matches the formula (verify-patterns.py).
B06.visual_intent: Code card at left (the stretched address, floor, the color line); at right a real Godot window: a square of sixteen flat-colored cells, red growing with the column and green with the row. The highlighted lines carry short labels: canvas_item, vec2, COLOR.
B06.motion_claim: The floor line is highlighted, then the color line, while sixteen flat cells sit in the window.

show.event: first line highlighted, label canvas_item: a shader for 2D drawing
stretch and floor lines highlighted, label vec2: a pair of numbers
COLOR line highlighted, label COLOR: the pixel's color; red and green steps traced across and down

B06.why: Code and its picture side by side is the claim: the same two numbers for every pixel of a cell.

B07.capture_spec: C03: Lab sprite, white texture, lab-shaders/03-cells-fract.gdshader, still PNG. Verified: all sixteen 90 px tiles of the 360x360 render are pixel-identical; the render matches the formula at every pixel.
B07.visual_intent: Code card at left; at right a real Godot window: the square of four by four cells again, but every cell holds the same small gradient (red growing left to right, green top to bottom), restarting at each border.
B07.motion_claim: The fract line, then the color line, are highlighted while sixteen identical gradients fill the window.

show.event: fract line highlighted
ring on one cell, then its copy in another
COLOR line highlighted

B07.why: Sixteen identical gradients are only convincing as a real render, with the code that makes them.

cues.label: texture(): read the picture at an address

B08.capture_spec: C04: Lab sprite (sprite texture), lab-shaders/04-tile.gdshader, still PNG. Verified: nine copies; tiles differ from the first by at most 21 of 9,216 pixels (edge pixels).
B08.visual_intent: Code card at left; at right a real Godot window: the teal test sprite repeated three times across and three down inside its square, the stage showing through its transparent padding.
B08.motion_claim: Nine copies of the sprite sit in a three by three grid; the fract line is highlighted, then the texture line.

show.event: fract line highlighted
texture line; the 3 by 3 grid of copies traced

B08.why: A tiled floor is best seen as the real result of two lines.

B09.visual_intent: A map diagram. At left a ramp strip splits (two drawn arrow shapes) into two panels. Panel one, title 'floor', text 'one per cell', with two small drawn icons: pixel blocks and a checkerboard. Panel two, title 'fract', text 'repeats', with two small drawn icons: diagonal stripes and a dot grid. Below, both panels send an arrow to one last icon, a dot screen, labelled 'both'. Midpoint still (45 to 55 %): the strip has split into the two panels and the floor panel is full (block and checker icons); the fract panel is still empty.
B09.motion_claim: The strip splits, each panel fills with its icons in turn, and the two arrows merge on the dot screen.

show.event: ramp strip splits into the two panels
floor panel: block and checker icons
fract panel: stripe and dot icons
arrows merge on the dot screen, label 'both'

B09.why: The point is a structure with a shape (two roles, one merge); drawn arrows and small pictures beat a card of words.
